angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 375,678 km at 147.72 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.7697 +/- 0.0282 mas (same row, RUWE 1.19): 147.72 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.54 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Gan et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-530 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.511...83G/abstract): 375,678 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.53 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Gan et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-530 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.511...83G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3659 +/- 120 K from Gan et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-530 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.511...83G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Gan et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-530 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.511...83G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-530.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.698, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
